questions.q: In the Sort transformation, what does a NEGATIVE sort order number mean for that column?
options: Sort that column in descending order
Sort that column in ascending order
Exclude that column from the output entirely
Sort that column before any positively-numbered columns, regardless of its number
questions.explain: A positive sort order number means ascending order; a negative number means descending order. A sort order of 0 means the column isn't sorted but is still passed through.

questions.q: If CountryRegion has sort order 1 and City has sort order 2, what is the resulting sort priority?
options: Sorted by CountryRegion first, then by City within each region
Sorted by City first, then by CountryRegion
Both columns sorted independently and merged afterward
Only CountryRegion is sorted; City's setting is ignored
questions.explain: The column with the lowest sort order number is sorted first; the column with the next lowest number breaks ties within that first sort — the same idea as ORDER BY CountryRegion, City in T-SQL.

questions.q: How does the Sort transformation remove duplicate rows?
options: Via a 'Remove rows with duplicate sort values' option applied during the same sort operation
It requires a separate Aggregate transformation chained afterward
It cannot remove duplicates under any configuration
By running the Conditional Split transformation on the sort keys
questions.explain: The Sort transformation includes a checkbox option to remove rows with duplicate sort values as part of the same sort pass — no separate transformation needed.

questions.q: Which two transformations, covered later in this chapter, specifically require their inputs to already be sorted?
options: Merge and Merge Join
Lookup and Conditional Split
Derived Column and Data Conversion
Aggregate and Derived Column
questions.explain: Both the Merge transformation and the Merge Join transformation require sorted input on the columns being merged or joined — the Sort transformation is how you guarantee that beforehand.

questions.q: What does a column with a sort order of 0 mean in the Sort transformation?
options: The column is not sorted, but is still copied through to the output
The column is sorted first, before every other column
The column is dropped from the output entirely
The column triggers descending sort automatically
questions.explain: Columns with a sort order of 0 are not part of the sort, but they are still automatically copied to the transformation output alongside the sorted columns.
